newsitem.title: USA: Strikes cut GM's Q4 N. American production.
newsitem.headline: Strikes cut GM's Q4 N. American production.

text.p: General Motors Corp said it reduced its fourth quarter North American production forecast by 151,000 cars and trucks because of strikes in the United States and Canada.

GM said as of the end of October, it expected to build 1,169,000 vehicles in the United States, Canada and Mexico during the fourth quarter. In the same period of 1995, GM built 1,372,000 vehicles in those countries.

GM spokesman Thomas Klipstine said the automaker lost production of about 113,000 passenger cars and 38,000 light trucks because of the strikes through October. But there may be further downward adjustments to GM's fourth quarter production plans because of estimates of lost production in the month of November.
"We could have a few more units lost," he said.
During the month of October, GM's North American Operations produced a total of 405,000 passenger cars and trucks in the United States, Canada and Mexico, including 197,000 cars and 208,000 trucks.
